findings.text: the §3 table builds each log path as "logs/enforced/" plus the full test filename plus ".log", so all nine rows cite files such as logs/enforced/test_a_context_refusal_names_the_window.py.log that do not exist (the real files are the same stem without ".py", and three cited tests have no per-file log at all), which makes the page's evidence column contradict the correct log list printed immediately above it.

the "reconcile the status word the other way too" rule at skills/reckon-build/references/worker-verification.md:144 is dispositioned "delete as enforced" on tests/test_manifest_parse_format.py::test_an_unknown_status_word_raises_naming_the_word_and_the_recognised, whose only assertion is a refusal of an invented vocabulary word and which never checks a valid complete against a run classification, so the done_when's "drives the guarded action far enough to make the check fire" is not met for that row.

sentences after the first in a paragraph are attributed to the line where the split landed rather than the line the sentence starts on, so 127 of 757 rows cite an earlier line (575 exact, the displaced rows 2 to 66 lines off; skills/reckon-build/references/worker-verification.md:144 is cited for a rule at line 151), which sends a reader following the locator to a different sentence.

it duplicates the binding-sentence scanner in docs/figures/the-crew-contract-fits-one-read/classify-rules-in-the-skill/scan_binding.py, carrying a near-identical KEYWORDS regex, IMPERATIVE_VERBS set and abbreviation guard, rather than extending that owner to the twelve-file corpus, so the two counters can disagree about the same text.
